codeReview.summary: Reviewed the current combined code for the public /reservations/* API, the operator large-party approve/decline routes, the App Sites gate, the RESERVATIONS_PUBLIC_ENABLED kill switch, the security sweep, and the two carried-over fixes. The feature meets its expectedBehavior and the VAL-ONLINE-001..041 requirements on the runtime the contract tests (Node tenant-api 3007/3009). Origin-only resolution (apps/tenant-api/src/lib/origin.ts:345-368, apps/tenant-api/workers/org-router.ts:222-231) plus the route gate in apps/tenant-api/src/lib/reservations-public-auth.ts:74-103 correctly fails closed with the uniform 404 for missing/unknown Origin, wrong region, unprovisioned org, master-flag-off and online-flag-off (manage/ics stay up); the kill switch is checked before origin resolution (line 80) and returns 503 only for public routes. Holds, idempotent booking, HMAC/HKDF-derived manage tokens (never stored; holds store sha256 only), per-phone limits, X-Client channel recording, POST-only mutations, honeypot, field-path-only validation and durable rsv_rate_counters limits all match architecture.md section 7.3 and are covered by reservations-public.test.ts (44 route tests), the real-SQLite concurrency tests (one winner on the last table, single hold conversion, idempotent replay) and the security sweep in reservations-security.test.ts. Every public write goes through withReservationWrite with engine re-validation inside the transaction and idempotency scoped by (scope, key, request_hash), so no double booking path was found; approve/decline run under withReservationWrite and are status-guarded (pending_approval only, 409 invalid_status_transition), and decline frees the held occupancies. Residency is respected: manager alerts carry ids/counts only (services/rsv-outbox.ts:33-42,51-83), the request log uses c.req.path with no query/body (lib/request-logging.ts:40-50), the App gate returns flags only, and validation/response bodies never echo submitted values. The carried-over fixes are correct: scale.test.ts now takes the median of 5 timed runs after a warm-up while keeping the 200/2000/5000 budget assertions untouched (packages/reservations/src/engine/scale.test.ts:17-30,44-46), and birthday/anniversary were added to RSV_TAG_SYSTEM_KEY_VALUES (packages/tenant-db/src/schema.ts:2948-2953) with the `as never` cast removed (apps/tenant-api/src/routes/reservations-book.test.ts:1492). Findings below are non-blocking: two are runtime/coverage nuances inherited from the shared /careers/ edge pattern, and one is a cross-feature retry nuance where the server follows the contract exactly.

issues.description: On the Cloudflare Workers runtime (the production US node per the repo AGENTS.md), a /reservations/* request whose Origin binds no organization never reaches the route handler: the edge answers `400 { error: 'Could not resolve tenant organization for this request' }` (workers/index.ts:307-312), and a wrong-region Origin (e.g. the riyadh-grill origin on the US worker) answers `409 region_mismatch` including `orgRegion`/`nodeRegion` via assertOrgOnUsNode (workers/org-router.ts:313-333). VAL-ONLINE-024/VAL-ONLINE-025 and this feature's expectedBehavior require the identical `404 { error: 'not_found' }` shape, which is what the Node runtime returns (the contract's tool: curl against 3007/3009, where resolvePublicOrg fails closed at lib/reservations-public-auth.ts:90-101). This is the pre-existing `/careers/` edge pattern the architecture told the worker to mirror, not new logic, and it discloses no guest data — but the feature's new org-router branch is what puts /reservations* on that path, so the deviation is worth an orchestrator decision (either accept it as platform behavior or have the edge answer 404 for /reservations*).

Coverage gap for a documented mission rule: the public-route security sweep (describe starting at line 1104) has no `hasProvisionedDb = false` case, although the gate implements it (lib/reservations-public-auth.ts:90) and AGENTS.md requires every reservations route to verify it. ORG_UNPROVISIONED exists in the same file (line 68) but is only registered for the operator block, whose sweep does assert the uniform 404 (line 499-520). The behavior itself is correct; only the public-route test is missing, so a future refactor of resolvePublicOrg could regress it unnoticed.

Idempotency is hashed over the whole submitted body (hashIdempotencyPayload(body.data), reservations-public.ts:625; lib/reservations-write.ts:184-188), and bookSchema accepts a `turnstileToken` field (line 198) that POST /reservations never verifies. This is exactly the approved contract (VAL-ONLINE-014 defines replay as a byte-identical body and requires 409 idempotency_conflict for any changed field), but it makes a real client retry fragile: the Sites flow keeps one Idempotency-Key per hold (apps/sites/src/lib/reservations/flow.ts:722) and resets the Turnstile challenge after every failed attempt (flow.ts:804,810,814), so a retry after a committed-but-lost response sends the same key with a different turnstileToken and receives 409 idempotency_conflict instead of the replayed confirmation. Server-side this is per contract; flagging so the Sites/native clients (or a later contract revision) can decide whether to exclude the unverified challenge token from the hash.

sharedStateObservations.observation: AGENTS.md's write-path rule says every versioned operator mutation (listing "reservation edits/status/notes/assign") sends and checks expectedVersion and returns 409 stale_version, but the new large-party approve/decline routes accept only { locationId?, reason? } and guard with a status precondition instead (409 invalid_status_transition). The App client matches (it sends no expectedVersion), so nothing is broken today, but the rule-vs-code mismatch will bite the next worker that adds a versioned route.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: apps/tenant-api/src/routes/operator-reservations-book.ts:1642-1645 (schema) and 1659-1665 (handler); apps/tenant-api/src/services/rsv-request-service.ts:58-60 and 159-161 (status guard); apps/app/app/utils/reservations/book-api.ts:2556-2578 (client sends no expectedVersion); mission AGENTS.md 'Write path' bullet.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The backend-worker skill's step 6 requires curl verification of every expectedBehavior against the running node. The worker skipped curl for operator approve/decline (needs an App-minted rsv+jwt, and the Requests-tab UI did not exist yet) and covered them with route tests instead. The deviation is justified, but the skill does not say what to do when the only way to obtain an operator token is another feature's UI.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The edge/runtime split for public Origin failures is not recorded anywhere: on Cloudflare Workers an unroutable Origin yields 400 and a wrong-region Origin yields 409 region_mismatch before any /reservations route runs, while the Node runtime yields the uniform 404. Validators or native workers who test against the Workers runtime (wrangler dev) would see a different shape than the contract's curl checks on 3007/3009.

summary: PASS. The online-booking backend implements the contract: Origin-only org resolution with region/flag checks and the uniform 404 (Node runtime), RESERVATIONS_PUBLIC_ENABLED answering 503 only on public routes, config/availability (ETag/dayVersion/now/alternatives/party limits/large-party/closed-vs-online-closed/staff-only exclusion) and the 62-day calendar, holds with countdown and replaceHoldToken, idempotent booking with 8-char Crockford codes and derived (never stored) manage tokens, per-phone limits, X-Client channel recording, manage modify/cancel/confirm/running-late/ics, /mine, large-party requests with operator approve/decline under withReservationWrite, the App Sites gate returning flags only, and the full security sweep. Residency holds: ids-and-counts-only cross-plane payloads, no PII in logs, field-path-only validation errors, sha256 hold tokens. The carried-over scale-test median fix keeps the 200/2000/5000 budget assertions, and birthday/anniversary were added to RSV_TAG_SYSTEM_KEY_VALUES with the `as never` cast removed. Three non-blocking findings: the Workers edge answers 400/409 (with region disclosure) instead of the uniform 404 before the route runs; the public security sweep lacks a hasProvisionedDb=false case even though the gate implements it; and the whole-body idempotency hash makes a Sites retry with a refreshed Turnstile token a 409 (per contract, but fragile). Four shared-state notes (approve/decline vs the expectedVersion rule, skill guidance for operator-token verification, the Workers-vs-Node 404 difference, and the now-automatic context refresh after set_org_flag) are recorded for the validator to triage.
